elements.description: No keyless route from GitHub Actions into the account (OIDC denied): deployments run from the owner's machine with a 12-hour aws login session. Phase 11 decides how CI deploys.

elements.description: Deliberate lockout of a known account (T-ID-10) is now bounded per IP (20 sign-in attempts per 2 minutes), but a distributed attacker can still trigger the per-account lockout. Edge bot controls (Phase 5) reduce it further. Accepted: lockout expires after 15 minutes.
elements.name: Deliberate lockout of a known account (T-ID-10) is now bounded per IP (20 sign-in attempts per 2 minutes), but a distributed attacker can still trigger the per-account lockout

elements.name: Rate-limit state is per database: a database outage disables sign-in entirely (fails closed).

elements.description: Correlation for audit-fed events (failed sign-ins, denials) runs inside the request that produced them (ADR-0018), so an attack burst adds a little latency to those requests; HTTP analysis runs after the response. Bounded by the rate limiter; revisited in Phase 12.
elements.name: Correlation for audit-fed events (failed sign-ins, denials) runs inside the request that produced them (ADR-0018), so an attack burst adds a little latency to those requests; HTTP analysis runs after

elements.description: On one machine every request comes from one address, so local detections group into a single incident. Expected; not a weakness of the deployed design.
elements.name: On one machine every request comes from one address, so local detections group into a single incident

elements.description: The Debian 13 base of the API image carries high OS package vulnerabilities with no fix published (44 at the end of Phase 8). They are reported on every scan and block as soon as a fix exists; most are in packages the service never executes. A minimal base image (distroless or Alpine) is planned with Phase 12 hardening.
elements.name: The Debian 13 base of the API image carries high OS package vulnerabilities with no fix published (44 at the end of Phase 8)

elements.description: The scan gate reads a committed file (scanning/accepted-findings.toml) generated from the approved exceptions (make accepted-risks). Between a decision and the next generation the gate uses the previous file; run it after every scan-finding decision. Finding-level risk acceptances (Phase 8) and exceptions remain two records with different scopes.
elements.name: The scan gate reads a committed file (scanning/accepted-findings.toml) generated from the approved exceptions (make accepted-risks)

elements.description: Permanently deleting an application threat model removes its rows; the audit log keeps a summary (counts and the first 50 threats), not the whole model. Archive is offered first.
elements.name: Permanently deleting an application threat model removes its rows; the audit log keeps a summary (counts and the first 50 threats), not the whole model

elements.description: Prompt-risk scoring is a set of patterns: it names likely injection attempts but can be evaded. It is a signal for the reviewer, not a defence; the defences are delimiting, the verbatim evidence contract and tighten-only proposals with human approval.
elements.name: Prompt-risk scoring is a set of patterns: it names likely injection attempts but can be evaded

elements.description: A model can still be wrong within the contract: a correct quote with a misleading inference. Inference is labelled, the platform's own verdict is never changed, and nothing runs without a lead's approval.
elements.name: A model can still be wrong within the contract: a correct quote with a misleading inference

elements.description: The offline analyser is deterministic and not a model; it proves the engine, not the quality of a real model's answers. Bedrock answers vary between runs (temperature 0 narrows, not removes).
elements.name: The offline analyser is deterministic and not a model; it proves the engine, not the quality of a real model's answers

elements.description: Limits are per day and counted from stored analyses; a burst within the limit is allowed. Bedrock spend is also bounded by the AWS budget alert the setup asks for.
elements.name: Limits are per day and counted from stored analyses; a burst within the limit is allowed

elements.description: The posture score is computed on request and snapshotted once a day on the first read; with no scheduler, a day nobody opens it has no snapshot.
elements.name: The posture score is computed on request and snapshotted once a day on the first read; with no scheduler, a day nobody opens it has no snapshot.
